habitat: Pairs and small groups on grassy watersides, riverbanks, dam walls and the fringes of sewage ponds and vleis.
summary: A common resident. The bill, wattles and legs are bright yellow. The wattles are shorter than those of the White-crowned Lapwing, and the white is only a patch on the forecrown. The neck is streaked, the folded wing has no white bar, the breast is brown and the belly is white. The upperparts are pale grey-brown. The call is a shrill kwep-kwep-kwep-kwep, speeding up when the bird is agitated.

similar.note: White-crowned Lapwing has longer wattles, a white crown-band, entirely white underparts and a black wing edged white.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^7=128 mature individuals (visiting breeder); paper interval half–double → 64–256.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

head.pattern: White patch only on the forecrown. Yellow wattles shorter than those of the White-crowned Lapwing. Neck streaked black.

upperparts.pattern: Pale grey-brown upperparts. No white bar on the folded wing.

calls.description: A shrill kwep-kwep-kwep-kwep, speeding up with increased agitation. The texts do not separate the sexes. Grade A from Kalwelwa, Zambia.
